Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer to the following question from the four alternatives given below.
In the past 50 years, doctors across the world have accepted the practice to prescribe antibiotics at the first sign of a trivial infection or treat patients with a handful of antibiotics. These days it is not uncommon to see practitioners prescribing multiple antibiotics without any real indication or relevance for such a combination of drugs. Antibiotics have traditionally been known as miracle drugs, but there is growing evidence that they are overworked miracles, especially in countries like ours where there is easy access to drugs across the counter, including antibiotics. We cannot think of a return to pre-antibiotic days. Yet the unbridled use of these agents is inexorably propelling us in that direction.
Antibiotics are called overworked miracles because:
questions.questionText: Read the passage carefully and choose the best answer to the following question from the four alternatives given below. In the past 50 years, doctors across the world have accepted the practice to prescribe antibiotics at the first sign of a trivial infection or treat patients with a handful of antibiotics. These days it is not uncommon to see practitioners prescribing multiple antibiotics without any real indication or relevance for such a combination of drugs. Antibiotics have traditionally been known as miracle drugs, but there is growing evidence that they are overworked miracles, especially in countries like ours where there is easy access to drugs across the counter, including antibiotics. We cannot think of a return to pre-antibiotic days. Yet the unbridled use of these agents is inexorably propelling us in that direction. Antibiotics are called overworked miracles because:
questions.explanationHtml:
(c)
The passage clearly points out that antibiotics are being excessively used, so they are called overworked miracles.

questions.subject: Civil Engineering
questions.questionMarkup:
During a temperature inversion in the atmosphere, the movement of air pollutants is restricted.
Under such conditions, how do the pollutants generally behave?
questions.questionText: During a temperature inversion in the atmosphere, the movement of air pollutants is restricted. Under such conditions, how do the pollutants generally behave?

options.html: Get trapped above the inversion layer
options.text: Get trapped above the inversion layer

options.html: Accumulate near the ground surface below the inversion layer.
options.text: Accumulate near the ground surface below the inversion layer.

options.html: Spread sideways in the horizontal direction
options.text: Spread sideways in the horizontal direction

options.html: Rise upward and mix with the upper layers
options.text: Rise upward and mix with the upper layers

questions.explanationHtml:
(b)
Under normal conditions, warm air rises, enabling vertical mixing and pollutants dispersion, but
inversion reverses this dynamics thereby leading to accumulation and stagnation of pollution
close to ground below the inversion layer.

questions.questionText: Which of the following errors in chaining is/are non-compensating error(s)?

options.html: Sag of the chain between supports
options.text: Sag of the chain between supports

options.html: Incorrect alignment of the chain, not along the survey line.
options.text: Incorrect alignment of the chain, not along the survey line.

options.html: Non-horizontal alignment of the chain on sloping terrain.
options.text: Non-horizontal alignment of the chain on sloping terrain.

options.html: Variation in chain length due to temperature.
options.text: Variation in chain length due to temperature.

questions.explanationHtml:
(a, b, c, d)
Compensating errors in chaining are those which are equally likely to be positive or negative and
thus tend to cancel each other out when measurements are repeated over long distances.
Non-compensating errors are one-sided; they always occur in the same direction.

options.html: Specific surface area of the medium governs the extent of biofilm growth.
options.text: Specific surface area of the medium governs the extent of biofilm growth.

options.html: Porosity of the medium facilitates both wastewater passage and ventilation of product gases.
options.text: Porosity of the medium facilitates both wastewater passage and ventilation of product gases.

options.html: Rotating distribution arms help in even distribution and air circulation through intermittent dosing.
options.text: Rotating distribution arms help in even distribution and air circulation through intermittent dosing.

options.html: The primary function of the medium is filtration of wastewater through granular pores.
options.text: The primary function of the medium is filtration of wastewater through granular pores.

questions.explanationHtml:
(d)
The term filter is misleading in trickling filters, since few of the physical processes associated
with filtration through granular media function in trickling filters. Instead, sorption and subsequent
biological oxidation are the primary means of food removal.
